statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of four public archetypes. The valid search-results template and authenticated upload/account flows were not covered because they were not required to complete the public watch journey; the invalid result URL was retained specifically as error-state evidence.

page.notes: Persian RTL public video platform. Core video entities hydrate client-side. CDN hostnames are classified as third-party by origin in HAR totals even when operationally first-party.

checkOutcomes.method: Paired emulated-media screenshots and DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Light and dark emulations produced distinct, usable complete color systems, and the mobile UI exposes a night-mode control.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, matchMedia was true, getAnimations() returned none and scroll-behavior was auto.
axe-core marked 24 home nodes for manual color-contrast review and found a definite contrast failure on the video ad banner; no forced-colors/high-contrast adaptation was detectable in loaded CSS.
The computed CSS probe found no view-transition rules on home or video despite client-side Next.js navigation between feed and detail templates.
Representative home, listing and video surfaces showed no scroll-linked decorative effect; CSS inspection found no animation-timeline/scroll-timeline and the page retains native scrolling.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile screenshot, layout metrics and interactive-element geometry probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile feed uses native vertical scrolling and direct touch-sized controls without a custom gesture-only core action.
Desktop keeps the active Home item highlighted in a stable sidebar, while mobile replaces it with a persistent bottom navigation and active item.
No tooltip or viewport-edge anchored overlay was part of the representative unauthenticated surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No anchored tooltip/popover was present to position.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Active navigation state, page H1 on video, selected home tab and prominent playback area provide clear orientation after navigation.
No modal or full-viewport interstitial obscured content on load; the mobile install banner is bounded at the bottom and has a visible close control.
axe-core found 15 home and 5 video aria-required-children violations plus 23 aria-required-parent violations; the DOM probe found no dialog, popover, or details elements.
Home prioritizes feed cards and video prioritizes the player/title; chrome remains limited to navigation and task controls.
At 360x800, scrollWidth, clientWidth and innerWidth were all 360 with 0 horizontal overflow; viewport meta is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Paired responsive screenshots and CSS feature probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The desktop/mobile screenshots show cards changing layout, but CSS inspection found no @container or container-type usage on either home or video templates.

checkOutcomes.method: Programmatic focus and computed outline probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focused the first visible button and computed outline as none with no box-shadow on both home and video.
Home clearly presents personalized videos, Shorts and categories; the detail page gives dominant placement to playback and its video title.

checkOutcomes.method: Cross-route walkthrough with home DOM links and video screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: A video linked from the home feed loaded into a playable detail page with title, channel, follow, save, share and recommendations.

checkOutcomes.method: Timed listing screenshot and explicit 404-state screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: After a 10-second wait, the representative /explore listing showed only a centered spinner with no status text, timeout, retry, or fallback content.
Mobile Lighthouse measured home LCP 7.9s, CLS 0.51 and TBT 610ms; video LCP was 16.9s with TBT 900ms. The trace corroborated home LCP 2.88s under a less constrained run.
The 360x800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.459, including a single 0.379 shift around 4.1s; Lighthouse independently measured 0.51.
Home trace found two long tasks up to 150ms and 132ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 610ms TBT on home and 900ms on video.
Home loaded 69 requests and 1.53MB with three VeryHigh parser stylesheets; video loaded 30.95MB in 10 seconds, while Lighthouse video LCP reached 16.9s.
Lighthouse estimated 424KiB unused JavaScript on home and 362KiB on video; analytics and several application chunks each waste 40% to 84%.
axe-core found unnamed buttons, an unnamed ARIA listbox, unnamed video links, 15 home required-child failures, 23 required-parent failures, and 17 nested interactive controls.
axe-core confirmed a serious color-contrast violation on the video banner and another on the error page, with 24 home nodes requiring review.
Home has no H1; axe found missing main landmark on the error template and semantic list/listitem defects, while focused primary buttons computed no visible outline.
Persian body and headings remain unclipped and readable in desktop, video and 360px screenshots with clear line spacing and hierarchy.

axe flagged video-caption as critical/manual on 12 home previews and the played video; the video element had zero caption/subtitle tracks. The error template also disabled text scaling according to axe.
Lighthouse captured a console.error TimeoutError during video API fetching from the client bundle.
The images primitive found all three video images missing width/height, two below-fold images not lazy, and legacy JPG delivery; home also had an undimensioned GIF.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and permission-state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found BFCache eligibility, valid image aspect ratios and crawlable anchors; no permission prompt appeared on load.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse SEO and direct head metadata probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse passed document titles but failed meta-description on both home and video; direct probes returned no description.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse, DOM links, layout and robots/sitemap probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse passed crawlable anchors, descriptive link text and robots.txt; viewport meta is present and robots exposes a sitemap.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw HTML discoverability comparison and metadata probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Discoverability fetched HTTP 200 but found 0% video content coverage, no raw title/H1, and crawler screenshots without the rendered entity; direct metadata probes found no canonical.
The representative video probe found no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter metadata despite a visible title, channel, playback media and engagement details.
Headers showed no Content-Security-Policy; cookie audit found seven flagged cookies, including insecure _ga cookies with SameSite=None and 400-day expiry.
Tracker capture found 11 third-party origins and Google Tag Manager/Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and Yandex; HAR attributed 28 requests and 676KB to third parties on home.
Notification permission remained default and no geolocation/notification prompt appeared on load; authentication was not required for the primary viewing flow.
HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and Referrer-Policy were present, but CSP and Permissions-Policy were absent.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw server HTML versus rendered-DOM discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The video discoverability comparison found 0% rendered-content coverage in raw HTML: raw text had no content tokens and omitted title and H1, while the rendered page had the full video entity.
Video recommendations, menus and mobile navigation remained within viewport bounds with no horizontal overflow; the dedicated error route rendered a stable state.
The document links a web app manifest and navigator.serviceWorker reported one active registration.
The invalid route rendered an explicit bilingual 404 state while preserving global search/navigation rather than a blank shell.
Both templates declare html lang=fa and dir=rtl, render RTL correctly, and loaded CSS contains logical inline/block properties.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered screenshot and DOM text review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible counts, dates and relative times are localized into the Persian-language RTL interface instead of exposing raw machine timestamps.
No scheduling, event-time, recurring-time or cross-zone workflow was present on the representative public video surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited paths do not expose time-zone-sensitive event data.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Core viewing works without login; sign-in is offered rather than forced, and no consent wall, confirmshaming, disguised ad control or forced continuity appeared.

checkOutcomes.method: Form inventory reported zero home forms
checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-submitted form with validation was part of the representative public viewing journey.
The search field has a visible Persian purpose and aria-label; it does not obstruct paste or force authentication for browsing.
No checkout, subscription purchase, consent decision, or account-management flow was present in the scoped unauthenticated journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No commercial or account-management commitment was in scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Images, HAR, tracker and Lighthouse evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: Image inspection found no dimensions or srcset on all tested images, two legacy JPGs on video, and a legacy GIF on home.

checkOutcomes.method: Images, HAR, tracker and Lighthouse evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home transferred 319KB from Google tag scripts plus 91KB Yandex and 26KB Clarity, while Lighthouse found large unused portions of those scripts.

checkOutcomes.method: Images, HAR, tracker and Lighthouse evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: The video page transferred 30.95MB in 10 seconds, including 29.65MB of 720p segments, while home loaded multiple tracker suites before user interaction.
No declared agent-facing intent or transactional agent surface was present; public crawler visibility is judged separately under discoverability/resilience.
checkOutcomes.reason: Emerging WebMCP capability is not a declared surface for this public video audit.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative browsing and playback tasks do not require an on-device language-model or summarizer feature.
checkOutcomes.reason: On-device inference is not necessary for the scoped core task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-feed scroll-down/up cycles, heap rose from 34,547,314 to 34,942,215 self-size bytes (about 1.1%) and nodes from 615,675 to 619,632, with no unbounded jump.
Heap summaries remained near 35MB self-size and about 620k heap nodes for a media feed, proportionate to the rendered long feed.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary constructor and total comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: The before/after heap constructor summaries did not show a material Detached* population increase, while total growth after ten cycles was about 1.1%.

principleOutcomes.reason: Emerging WebMCP capability is not a declared surface for this public video audit. On-device inference is not necessary for the scoped core task.

paths.description: Public home/feed archetype at desktop and 360px mobile; covers discovery, feed browsing, theme, responsive layout and repeated scrolling.
Representative video-detail and playback journey reached from the home feed; covers the core watch task, media, recommendations and metadata.
Channel/listing archetype linked from primary navigation; tested for loading and recovery behavior.
Invalid result route used as the representative not-found/recovery state, not as a valid search-results test.

findings.summary: High-contrast robustness and normal contrast have unresolved failures
findings.evidence: axe-core marked 24 home nodes for manual color-contrast review and found a definite contrast failure on the video ad banner; no forced-colors/high-contrast adaptation was detectable in loaded CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Define forced-colors/prefers-contrast states, preserve system colors for controls, and fix the confirmed low-contrast banner text.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: The computed CSS probe found no view-transition rules on home or video despite client-side Next.js navigation between feed and detail templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document View Transitions around client-side route/state changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Custom rich controls have broken ARIA structures instead of robust platform semantics
findings.evidence: axe-core found 15 home and 5 video aria-required-children violations plus 23 aria-required-parent violations; the DOM probe found no dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace transient menus/disclosures with popover, dialog, or details as appropriate and preserve the required ARIA ownership structure for composite widgets.

findings.summary: Responsive cards rely on viewport layout without container-level adaptation
findings.evidence: The desktop/mobile screenshots show cards changing layout, but CSS inspection found no @container or container-type usage on either home or video templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable feed and recommendation components containment and size-aware @container rules where they appear in different sidebars/grids.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on primary controls
findings.evidence: The focus probe programmatically focused the first visible button and computed outline as none with no box-shadow on both home and video.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment with sufficient contrast and preserve it for every button, link, and composite control.

findings.summary: The channel explore route remains an unlabeled spinner
findings.evidence: After a 10-second wait, the representative /explore listing showed only a centered spinner with no status text, timeout, retry, or fallback content.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose an accessible loading status, time out failed loads, and offer retry/back/recommended-channel recovery while preserving already available navigation.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are poor on key templates
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured home LCP 7.9s, CLS 0.51 and TBT 610ms; video LCP was 16.9s with TBT 900ms. The trace corroborated home LCP 2.88s under a less constrained run.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP discovery and render dependencies, reserve feed geometry, and prioritize only the critical visual and interaction work.

findings.summary: The home feed shifts substantially while loading
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer recorded CLS 0.459, including a single 0.379 shift around 4.1s; Lighthouse independently measured 0.51.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic space for feed modules, images, banners and personalized sections before their data arrives.

findings.summary: Long tasks delay interactivity
findings.evidence: Home trace found two long tasks up to 150ms and 132ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 610ms TBT on home and 900ms on video.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long initialization work into prioritized tasks and defer analytics and offscreen module hydration.

findings.summary: Resource delivery delays critical content and over-fetches media
findings.evidence: Home loaded 69 requests and 1.53MB with three VeryHigh parser stylesheets; video loaded 30.95MB in 10 seconds, while Lighthouse video LCP reached 16.9s.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical CSS/dependency chains, preload the actual LCP asset, and make video segment fetching adaptive to playback state and buffer need.

findings.summary: Hundreds of KiB of JavaScript are unused during initial use
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 424KiB unused JavaScript on home and 362KiB on video; analytics and several application chunks each waste 40% to 84%.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by template and interaction, load analytics after consent/idle, and remove duplicate tag-manager and unused vendor paths.

findings.summary: Critical names, roles and widget relationships fail across templates
findings.evidence: axe-core found unnamed buttons, an unnamed ARIA listbox, unnamed video links, 15 home required-child failures, 23 required-parent failures, and 17 nested interactive controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name, repair composite widget ownership, and avoid nesting controls inside links/cards.

findings.summary: Some text fails WCAG AA contrast
findings.evidence: axe-core confirmed a serious color-contrast violation on the video banner and another on the error page, with 24 home nodes requiring review.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/surface tokens to meet WCAG AA in both themes and test dynamic/ad content too.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark and focus structure is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Home has no H1; axe found missing main landmark on the error template and semantic list/listitem defects, while focused primary buttons computed no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1 per template, consistent main/nav landmarks, valid list structures, and a visible logical focus sequence.

findings.summary: Media equivalents and zoom support are incomplete
findings.evidence: axe flagged video-caption as critical/manual on 12 home previews and the played video; the video element had zero caption/subtitle tracks. The error template also disabled text scaling according to axe.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide accurate caption/subtitle tracks and remove any maximum-scale/user-scalable restriction from all template viewport declarations.

findings.summary: The primary video page logs a client-side API timeout
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a console.error TimeoutError during video API fetching from the client bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle expected timeout paths without console errors, show a recoverable UI state, and add bounded retry/telemetry.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery hints
findings.evidence: The images primitive found all three video images missing width/height, two below-fold images not lazy, and legacy JPG delivery; home also had an undimensioned GIF.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, lazy-load below-fold images, and provide srcset/sizes with modern formats.

findings.summary: Public templates omit meta descriptions
findings.evidence: Lighthouse passed document titles but failed meta-description on both home and video; direct probes returned no description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add unique descriptions that summarize each template and video without keyword stuffing.

findings.summary: Rendered video content is absent from raw HTML and lacks canonical signals
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched HTTP 200 but found 0% video content coverage, no raw title/H1, and crawler screenshots without the rendered entity; direct metadata probes found no canonical.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the visible video title/entity and canonical URL, and keep robots/sitemap signals consistent with those canonical pages.

findings.summary: Video pages expose no structured or social-preview metadata
findings.evidence: The representative video probe found no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter metadata despite a visible title, channel, playback media and engagement details.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate VideoObject JSON-LD plus Open Graph/Twitter video metadata matching the visible page.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but CSP and cookie posture are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers showed no Content-Security-Policy; cookie audit found seven flagged cookies, including insecure _ga cookies with SameSite=None and 400-day expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and set Secure plus appropriate Lax/Strict SameSite and proportionate lifetimes on first-party analytics cookies.

findings.summary: The public home page starts a broad tracking stack by default
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 11 third-party origins and Google Tag Manager/Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and Yandex; HAR attributed 28 requests and 676KB to third parties on home.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors and event scope, gate non-essential trackers behind informed consent, batch events, and avoid full-session analytics by default.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy coverage is incomplete
findings.evidence: HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and Referrer-Policy were present, but CSP and Permissions-Policy were absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP/frame-ancestors policy and a Permissions-Policy that disables unneeded capabilities; assess Trusted Types for the client app.

findings.summary: Core public content requires JavaScript
findings.evidence: The video discoverability comparison found 0% rendered-content coverage in raw HTML: raw text had no content tokens and omitted title and H1, while the rendered page had the full video entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core feed/video text and real links so browsing and entity understanding work before hydration and without JavaScript.

findings.summary: Asset delivery misses basic responsive-image optimizations
findings.evidence: Image inspection found no dimensions or srcset on all tested images, two legacy JPGs on video, and a legacy GIF on home.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where effective, provide srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and avoid GIF for animated UI art when video/animated WebP is lighter.

findings.summary: Multiple analytics systems consume bytes and background work
findings.evidence: Home transferred 319KB from Google tag scripts plus 91KB Yandex and 26KB Clarity, while Lighthouse found large unused portions of those scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant analytics, defer non-essential collection until idle/consent, and batch the minimum events needed.

findings.summary: Video and third-party budgets are disproportionate to the initial state
findings.evidence: The video page transferred 30.95MB in 10 seconds, including 29.65MB of 720p segments, while home loaded multiple tracker suites before user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use conservative adaptive startup quality and bounded buffering, pause segment fetch when not needed, and enforce vendor/media transfer budgets.

taskList.title: Restore semantic accessibility, focus, captions and contrast
Server-render and describe public video entities
Reduce tracking and harden browser policies
Bound video/media transfer and optimize images
